sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Texas City, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. Texas City homeowners can sell through a listing, to a cash buyer, or in a quick as-is sale, and a house with flood history, deferred repairs or a title problem often suits a buyer who does not need a mortgage.

The city sits on the southwestern shore of Galveston Bay in Galveston County, which shapes both the buyer pool and the questions buyers ask. Expect them to ask about flood history, drainage, insurance and the age of the roof. Gathering that paperwork early speeds up any route.

  • Listing with an agent: best exposure, with inspections and lender timelines.
  • Cash sale as is: fewer contingencies and a closing date you choose.
  • Delayed sale: possible when you need time to move or to settle an estate.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Texas City and its housing?
sections.html:
Texas City grew around a deepwater port. The Handbook of Texas says three brothers from Duluth, Minnesota, bought 10,000 acres of bay frontage in 1891, the first townsite plat was filed on May 17, 1893, and the city incorporated on September 16, 1911.

Refineries arrived after 1908, and the Handbook credits wartime industry and the port with the city's mid-century growth, from 16,620 people in 1950 to 32,065 in 1960. On April 16, 1947, a ship loaded with ammonium nitrate exploded in the harbor, killing 576 people and injuring more than 4,000. Hurricane Carla in 1961 brought four feet of floodwater over much of the city.

That history explains two local facts. The city grew fast in the 1940s and 1950s, so ask your own deed and permit records how old the house is and what has been updated. And the flood protection works, a barrier seawall begun in 1962 and finished in 1985 plus an eight-foot inner levee on Moses Lake built in 1982, are part of how buyers think about risk.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Texas City homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 59,733 residents in the July 2025 estimate, a rise of 15.2 percent from the 2020 base. A growing city draws buyers, which helps a seller who prices in line with local sales.

sections.h2: What draws buyers to Texas City?
sections.html:
Jobs, schools and water views draw them. The Handbook of Texas describes ten major refining and petrochemical industries forming the base of the port, and the city's growth running west from the bay.

It also lists civic amenities a buyer can use: the Nessler Civic Center, a 55-acre tract holding the city's largest park, library, city hall and stadium; the Texas City Dike, which extends into Galveston Bay; and Moses Lake, both developed as recreation areas. Texas City Independent School District dates to July 11, 1905, and College of the Mainland opened in September 1967.

  • Industrial shift workers value a short drive to the plants and port.
  • Commuters toward Houston or Galveston weigh the 25.7-minute average commute in the Census data.
  • Families look at the school district and park access.

Pointing to these features in your listing or offer conversation gives a buyer reasons beyond price.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Texas City and what should I know?
sections.html:
Galveston Central Appraisal District appraises Texas City property, and its customer service office is at 9850 Emmett F. Lowry Expressway, Suite A101, Texas City, TX 77591. Its listed hours are Monday through Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., and Friday, 8:00 a.m. to noon. Its phone number is (409) 935-1980.

Exemption applications can be mailed, filed online or brought to that office, and GCAD says it acts within 90 days of receipt. If you are denied, you are told and can protest. A disabled owner can qualify under the Social Security definition even without receiving benefits, and the school tax ceiling can move with you to a new qualifying Texas home.

  • Texas bills go out around October 1 and taxes are delinquent after January 31.
  • On February 1 a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.
  • The lien attaches on January 1, so a buyer needs those taxes settled for clear title.

Ask the Galveston County tax office for a payoff figure through your closing date.

sections.h2: How do I protest an appraisal in Galveston County?
sections.html:
File with GCAD, online or in writing, by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later. GCAD's pages describe an online protest through its taxpayer portal, where you can submit evidence, and informal meetings with an appraiser before any formal hearing.

The Comptroller adds that owners who appeal past the review board can go to district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values over $1,000,000. Anyone appealing must generally pay at least the undisputed tax before it goes delinquent.

Texas also caps homestead appraised value increases at 10 percent a year, starting the year after the exemption is first qualified. Ask GCAD how the cap applies to a buyer, since a realistic tax estimate helps buyers decide.

sections.h2: What flood and condition questions should I answer before selling in Texas City?
sections.html:
Prepare a clear answer for each. Buyers will ask whether the house has taken on water, whether it has a repair history, and what insurance it carries.

  • Gather insurance claim records, repair invoices and any elevation certificate you hold.
  • Photograph the roof, slab, drains and electrical panel.
  • Note whether the property has had foundation work and keep the paperwork.
  • Ask the city permit office whether past repairs were permitted.

A cash buyer who accepts the house as is will weigh these items in the price rather than demand that you fix them, but written records still help the offer.

sections.h2: What about foreclosure, inheritance or tenants in a Texas City sale?
sections.html:
For foreclosure, Texas auctions take place on the first Tuesday of the month with at least 21 days' notice, and you may reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days of the default notice. Selling before the auction can preserve equity.

For an inherited house, probate generally must be opened within four years of death, and a transfer on death deed recorded before death can pass the property without court. For tenants, the notice to vacate is at least three days unless the lease says otherwise, followed by a justice court case. The deed is recorded with the Galveston County Clerk, where the property lies, after a notary acknowledges the signature.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix flood damage before selling my Texas City house?
faqs.a: No. You can sell as is to a cash buyer, who will price the repairs. Disclose what you know and keep repair and insurance records, since buyers will ask for them.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about my Texas City appraisal?
faqs.a: Galveston Central Appraisal District, at its Texas City office or by phone at (409) 935-1980. The protest deadline is May 15 or 30 days after your notice, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Is there a state transfer tax when I sell in Texas City?
faqs.a: Ask your title company. The county clerk pages describe recording fees, so your closing statement is where any charges show up.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Texas City house that I inherited?
faqs.a: Often yes. You need legal authority to sign, which could come from an executor's deed, a muniment of title or a recorded transfer on death deed. Confirm with a Texas probate attorney.

faqs.q: How soon can a Texas City sale close?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close as fast as the title work allows, often within a few weeks, while a financed sale depends on the buyer's lender. Liens and back taxes can slow either path.
